entries.title: I Kings 18:3
segments: The fidelity and usefulness of truly religious persons sometimes lead very wicked men to employ them in preference to all others; and good men should ever strive so to act as to show that godliness is profitable unto all things, and that it renders those who possess it conscientiously diligent and faithful in the discharge of all the duties of life.

entries.title: I Kings 18:4
segments: Under the government of wicked rulers the Lord's ministers are often persecuted, imprisoned, and dependent on charity for support, while Satan's ministers go at large, and riot in luxury and abundance.

entries.title: I Kings 18:9
segments: Even the people of God are sometimes afraid to do what he commands them, lest they should suffer; but if they are truly devoted to him, and desirous of doing their duty, he will make it plain and enable them by his grace to perform it.

entries.title: I Kings 18:10
segments: No nation or kingdom; in that vicinity, or connected with Israel.

entries.title: I Kings 18:17
segments: Persecutors are apt to represent those who condemn them for their wickedness as disturbers of the public peace and troublers of the people, and to contend that their liberty is inconsistent with the public good, and that they should be banished or put to death.

entries.title: I Kings 18:18
segments:
Baalim; images of Baal. 
 
The troubles which come upon rulers and people are a punishment from God on account of their sins.  Not those who condemn these sins, but those who commit them, are the real troublers of the country.

entries.title: I Kings 18:19
segments:
Mount Carmel; a mountain near the Mediterranean, and south of the bay of Acre. 
 
  Of the groves; or, of Asherah, the same as Ashtoreth.

entries.title: I Kings 18:21
segments:
Halt ye; act as if doubtful whether Jehovah or Baal were the true God. 
 
As Jehovah has in various ways shown conclusively that he is the only living and true God, reason, interest, and duty require that all to whom he is revealed should, without hesitation or reserve, love, worship, and obey him.

entries.title: I Kings 18:22
segments:
I only; he was the only prophet of Jehovah who was present, or appeared before the people. 
 
Which is the right way is not to be determined by the numbers, wealth, and power of those who follow it.  God's friends may be few, poor, feeble, and despised, while Satan's may be many, rich, powerful, and respected.  It is better, in such cases, to be of the few than of the many.

entries.title: I Kings 18:24
segments: Let him be God; let him be acknowledged and adored as God.

entries.title: I Kings 18:26
segments: Leaped; as was the custom with idolaters.

entries.title: I Kings 18:27
segments:
He is a god; spoken in irony, intimating the absurdity of idol-worship. 
 
The worship of images, and of all false, imaginary deities, is mean, base, and foolish.

entries.title: I Kings 18:28
segments: The worship of false gods is cruel to the worshippers, and often leads to the infliciton of great bodily penances and sufferings.  Such sufferings please the tormentors, but do the tormented no good; and are an abomination to Jehovah, whose ways are ways of pleasantness, and whose paths are paths of peace.

entries.title: I Kings 18:29
segments: The time of the offering; about three o'clock in the afternoon, or between that and sunset.

entries.title: I Kings 18:32
segments: Two measures; a measure was about ten quarts.

entries.title: I Kings 18:33
segments: True religion has nothing to fear from experiment, and from candid, thorough, and searching investigation.  It loves the light, and seeks to diffuse it among all classes of people, so that they may be able to judge of it themselves, and act intelligently with regard to it.

entries.title: I Kings 18:37
segments:
Turned their heart; to worship Jehovah as the true God. 
 
Prayer, simple, earnest, and sincere, not in a foreign tongue which is not understood, but in that which the hearers themselves speak, is a powerful means of grace, and one by which God often convinces men of the truth and leads them to embrace it.

entries.title: I Kings 18:40
segments:
The brook Kishon; which emptied into the bay of Acre near the foot of mount Carmel. 
 
  Slew them; according to the command of God.

entries.title: I Kings 18:42
segments: Went up; from the brook Kishon to a place where refreshments were provided for him.

entries.title: I Kings 18:43
segments: Not only sincerity and earnestness, but perseverance in supplication and obedience to God, are essential to the highest success.  However small the number or trying the condition of the friends of Jehovah, let them trust in him, seek of him what they need, and follow his directions, and they shall in due time gloriously triumph over all their foes.

entries.title: I Kings 18:44
segments: Get thee down; from the mountain where he was, and return to his palace at Jezreel.

entries.title: I Kings 18:46
segments:
The hand of the Lord was on Elijah; imparting to him supernatural strength. 
 
  Girded up his loins; put a girdle or belt around his outer garments, as was the custom when about to travel. 
 
  Ran before Ahab; after the manner of royal attendants, that he might thus publicly honor him as the king of Israel.
